He played [[college basketball]] for the [[UNLV Runnin' Rebels basketball|UNLV Runnin' Rebels]]. ==High school career== For the first three years of his high school career, Vaughn attended [[Robbinsdale Cooper High School]] in [[New Hope, Minnesota]]. As a junior in 2012–13, he averaged 28 points and nine rebounds per game. For his senior year, he transferred to [[Findlay Prep]] in [[Henderson, Nevada]], where he averaged 19.9 points and 4.9 assists per game in 2013–14. He subsequently earned [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]] honors and Jordan Brand Classic selection.{{cite web|title=Rashad Vaughn Bio|url=http://www.unlvrebels.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/rashad_vaughn_906680.html|work=UNLVRebels.com|access-date=April 7, 2015|archive-date=June 26, [[Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball|Iowa State]], [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]], [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]] and [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina]], Vaughn finally committed to [[UNLV Runnin' Rebels basketball|UNLV]].{{cite web | url=http://collegebasketballtalk.nbcsports.com/2014/02/11/five-star-shooting-guard-rashad-vaughn-commits-to-unlv/ | title=Five-star shooting guard Rashad Vaughn commits to UNLV | publisher=NBC Sports | date=February 11, 2014 | access-date=July 28, 2015 | author=Payne, Terrence}}{{cite web | url=http://www.cbssports.com/collegebasketball/eye-on-college-basketball/24439594/top-10-recruit-rashad-vaughn-chooses-unlv-over-iowa-state | title=Top recruit Rashad Vaughn chooses UNLV over Iowa State | work=CBS Sports | date=February 11, 2014 | access-date=July 28, 2015 | author=Borzello, Jeff}} Vaughn played one season of college basketball for [[UNLV Runnin' Rebels basketball|UNLV]] where he was named the [[Mountain West Conference]] Freshman of the Year after averaging 17.8 points and 4.8 rebounds in 23 games.{{cite web|title=Rashad Vaughn 2015}} ==Professional career== ===Milwaukee Bucks (2015–2018)=== On June 25, 2015, Vaughn was selected by the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] with the 17th overall pick in the [[2015 NBA draft]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/bucks/features/boeder-ten-things-to-know-about-rashad-vaughn|title=10 THINGS TO KNOW ABOUT RASHAD VAUGHN|date=June 26, 2015|work=NBA.com|access-date=June 26, 2015}} He later joined the Bucks for the [[2015 NBA Summer League]]{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/bucks/release/bucks-announce-2015-summer-league-roster|title=BUCKS ANNOUNCE 2015 SUMMER LEAGUE ROSTER|date=July 1, 2015|work=NBA.com|access-date=July 13, 2015}} and signed his rookie scale contract with the team on July 17.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/bucks/release/bucks-sign-first-round-pick-rashad-vaughn|title=BUCKS SIGN FIRST ROUND PICK RASHAD VAUGHN|date=July 17, 2015|work=NBA.com|access-date=July 17, 2015}} He made his debut for the Bucks in the team's season opener against the [[New York Knicks]] on October 28, scoring 10 points off the bench in a 122–97 loss.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151028/NYKMIL/gameinfo.html|title=Williams scores 24, Knicks beat Bucks 122–97 in opener|work=NBA.com|date=October 28, 2015|access-date=October 28, 2015}} On March 18, 2016, pursuant to the flexible assignment rule, he was assigned to the [[Canton Charge]], the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]]' [[NBA Development League|D-League]] affiliate.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/bucks/release/bucks-assign-rashad-vaughn-canton-charge|title=BUCKS ASSIGN RASHAD VAUGHN TO CANTON CHARGE|work=NBA.com|date=March 18, 2016|access-date=March 18, 2016}} On March 26, he was recalled by the Bucks.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/bucks/release/bucks-recall-rashad-vaughn-canton-charge|title=BUCKS RECALL RASHAD VAUGHN FROM CANTON CHARGE|work=NBA.com|date=March 26, 2016|access-date=March 26, 2016}} On October 29, 2016, Vaughn scored a career-high 22 points and hit six three-pointers in a 110–108 win over the [[Brooklyn Nets]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899481|title=Henson's tip-in at buzzer leads Bucks past Nets|work=ESPN.com|date=October 29, 2016|access-date=October 30, 2016}} On November 19, pursuant to the flexible assignment rule, he was assigned to the [[Westchester Knicks]]{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/bucks/news/bucks-assign-rashad-vaughn-westchester-knicks|title=BUCKS ASSIGN RASHAD VAUGHN TO THE WESTCHESTER KNICKS|work=NBA.com|date=November 19, 2016|access-date=November 21, 2016}} and was recalled four days later.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/bucks/bucks-recall-rashad-vaughn-westchester-knicks|title=BUCKS RECALL RASHAD VAUGHN FROM WESTCHESTER KNICKS|work=NBA.com|date=November 23, 2016|access-date=November 26, 2016}} On November 26, he was reassigned to Westchester{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/bucks/bucks-assign-rashad-vaughn-westchester-knicks|title=BUCKS ASSIGN RASHAD VAUGHN TO WESTCHESTER KNICKS|work=NBA.com|date=November 26, 2016|access-date=November 26, 2016}} and recalled on December 1.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/bucks/release/bucks-recall-rashad-vaughn-westchester-knicks|title=BUCKS RECALL RASHAD VAUGHN FROM WESTCHESTER KNICKS|work=NBA.com|date=December 1, 2016|access-date=December 2, 2016}} ===Brooklyn Nets (2018)=== On February 5, 2018, Vaughn was traded, along with a second-round pick, to the [[Brooklyn Nets]] in exchange for [[Tyler Zeller]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/nets/news/2018/02/05/brooklyn-nets-acquire-rashad-vaughn-and-second-round-draft-pick-milwaukee|title=BROOKLYN NETS ACQUIRE RASHAD VAUGHN AND SECOND ROUND DRAFT PICK FROM MILWAUKEE|work=NBA.com|date=February 5, 2018|access-date=February 5, 2018}} He made his debut for the Nets the following day, collecting one assist in four minutes against the [[Houston Rockets]].{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/v/vaughra01/gamelog/2018/|title=Rashad Vaughn 2017–18 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=February 8, 2018}} On February 8, 2018, Vaughn was traded to the [[New Orleans Pelicans]] in exchange for [[Dante Cunningham]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/pelicans/pelicans-acquire-rashad-vaughn|title=Pelicans acquire Rashad Vaughn|work=NBA.com|date=February 8, 2018|access-date=February 8, 2018}} He was waived by the Pelicans two days later.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/article/2018/02/10/new-orleans-pelicans-waive-rashad-vaughn-mike-james#/|title=New Orleans Pelicans waive Rashad Vaughn, Mike James|work=NBA.com|date=February 10, 2018|access-date=February 13, 2018}} ===Orlando Magic (2018)=== On February 20, 2018, Vaughn signed a 10-day contract with the [[Orlando Magic]].{{cite web|last=Denton|first=John|url=http://www.nba.com/magic/news/magic-sign-rashad-vaughn-10-day-contract-20180220|title=Magic Sign Rashad Vaughn to 10-Day Contract|work=NBA.com|date=February 20, 2018|access-date=February 20, 2018}} He signed a second 10-day contract with the Magic on March 2,{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/magic/news/magic-sign-rashad-vaughn-second-10-day-contract-20180302|title=Magic Sign Rashad Vaughn to Second 10-Day Contract|work=NBA.com|date=March 2, 2018|access-date=March 2, 2018}} only to be waived by the team five days later due to injury.{{cite web|last=Robbins|first=Josh|url=http://www.orlandosentinel.com/sports/orlando-magic/os-sp-orlando-magic-notes-0308-story.html|title=Magic waive Rashad Vaughn, likely will sign Rodney Purvis to 10-day contract|work=OrlandoSentinel.com|date=March 7, 2018|access-date=March 7, 2018}} ===Texas Legends (2018)=== On October 8, 2018, the Mavericks announced they signed Vaughn to a training camp deal.{{cite web|url=https://www.mavs.com/mavericks-sign-donte-ingram-and-rashad-vaughn/amp/|title=Mavericks sign Vaughn and Ingram|work=mavs.com|date=October 8, 2018|access-date=October 8, 2018}} He was waived three days later.{{cite web|title=Mavericks Release Rashad Vaughn, Donte Ingram|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2018/10/mavericks-release-rashad-vaughn-donte-ingram.html|work=Mavs.com|date=October 11, 2018|access-date=October 11, 2018}} He then was added to the roster of the [[Texas Legends]], the Mavericks’ G League affiliate. ===Delaware Blue Coats (2018–2019)=== On December 31, 2018, Vaughn, alongside a 2019 third-round draft pick, was traded to the [[Delaware Blue Coats]] for the returning player rights to [[Askia Booker]] and a 2019 second-round pick.{{cite web |title=Blue Coats Acquire Rashad Vaughn from Texas Legends |url=https://bluecoats.gleague.nba.com/news/blue-coats-acquire-rashad-vaughn-from-texas-legends/ |website=NBA G League |access-date=December 31, 2018 |date=December 31, 2018 |archive-date=January 1, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190101051750/https://bluecoats.gleague.nba.com/news/blue-coats-acquire-rashad-vaughn-from-texas-legends/ |url-status=dead }} ===Igokea (2019–2020)=== On July 30, 2019, Vaughn signed a one-year contract for [[KK Igokea|Igokea]] of the [[ABA League|Adriatic League]].{{cite web |title=Rashad Vaughn is the new Igokea player |url=https://www.aba-liga.com/news.php?id=42131 |website=aba-liga.com |access-date=30 July 2019}} He averaged 16.5 points per game. ===Budućnost VOLI (2020)=== On June 7, 2020, he signed with [[KK Budućnost|Budućnost]].{{cite news |title=KK Buducnost signs Rashad Vaughn |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/kk-buducnost-signs-rashad-vaughn/ |website=Sportando |access-date=June 7, 2020 |date=June 7, 2020|last1=Carchia |first1=Emiliano }} On October 23, Budućnost and Vaughn parted ways after he appeared in six games.{{cite news |title=Buducnost, Rashad Vaughn agree to part ways |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/buducnost-rashad-vaughn-agree-to-part-ways/ |website=Sportando |access-date=October 23, 2020 |date=October 23, 2020|last1=Borghesan |first1=Ennio Terrasi }} ===Prometey (2020–2021)=== On December 22, 2020, he has signed with [[BC Prometey|Prometey]] of the [[Ukrainian Basketball SuperLeague]].{{Cite news|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/rashad-vaughn-signs-with-prometey/|title=Rashad Vaughn signs with Prometey|date=December 22, 2020|newspaper=Sportando|language=En|access-date=August 12, 2021|last1=Maggi |first1=Alessandro }} ===Dnipro (2021)=== On August 12, 2021, he has signed with [[BC Dnipro|Dnipro]] of the [[Ukrainian Basketball SuperLeague]].{{Cite news|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/bc-dnipro-sign-rashad-vaughn-rawle-alkins/|title=BC Dnipro sign Rashad Vaughn, Rawle Alkins|date=August 12, 2021|newspaper=Sportando|language=En|access-date=August 12, 2021|last1=Skerletic |first1=Dario }} Vaughn averaged 12.2 points, 4 rebounds and 1.6 assists per game. He parted ways with the team on November 28.{{cite news |title=BC Dnipro, Rashad Vaughn part ways |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/bc-dnipro-rashad-vaughn-part-ways/ |website=Sportando |access-date=November 28, 2021 |date=November 28, 2021|last1=Skerletic |first1=Dario }} ===Lavrio (2022)=== On January 28, 2022, Vaughn signed with [[G.S. Lavrio B.C.|Lavrio]] of the [[Greek Basket League]] and the [[Basketball Champions League]].{{cite web |last1=Mammides |first1=Chris |title=Rashad Vaughn (ex Dnipro) agreed terms with Lavrio |url=https://www.eurobasket.com/Greece/news/725653/Rashad-Vaughn-(ex-Dnipro)-agreed-terms-with-Lavrio |website=Eurobasket |access-date=January 9, 2022 |date=January 9, 2022}} In 12 league games, he averaged 14.4 points, 4.6 rebounds and 1 assist in 25 minutes per game. ===Cleveland Charge (2022–2023)=== On October 24, 2022, Vaughn joined the [[Cleveland Charge]] training camp roster.{{cite web|title=Charge 2022 Training Camp Roster|url=https://canton.gleague.nba.com/news/charge-2022-training-camp-roster/|website=NBA.com|date=October 24, 2022|access-date=October 24, 2022}} ===Apollon Patras (2023–2024)=== On November 20, 2023, Vaughn signed with [[Apollon Patras B.C.|Apollon Patras]] of the [[Greek Basket League]].{{cite news|first=Dario|last=Skerletic|title=Apollon Patras BC signs Rashad Vaughn|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/apollon-patras-bc-signs-rashad-vaughn/|newspaper=Sportando|date=November 20, 2023|access-date=January 21, 2024}} On January 29, 2024, Vaughn
